payload.baseline:
Four elements plus two standing constraints, taken from the winner's clustering - nothing redrawn.

E1 THE GATEKEEPER (engine/phone.ts, entry to the announce path). Black box: given an offer and who will adjudicate it, decides whether anything is sent at all and produces the current pairing. Says nothing about how. Carries F1, F2.

E2 THE BRIEF PIPELINE (a new module, engine/brief.ts). Black box: given an offer, yields either a URL whose fragment carries its key and which is CONFIRMED to serve, or nothing at all - and it never throws its failure at its caller. Internally: compose, encrypt, place, confirm, bound the lifetime. Carries F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F12.

E3 THE SUMMONS (engine/phone.ts, the card builder and publisher). Black box: given an offer, the pairing, and optionally a brief URL, produces one card that names the gate, carries answerable actions with absolute URLs, and includes the brief when there is one - and it fires whether or not E2 produced anything. Carries F8, F9, F10, F11.

E4 THE ANSWER READER (engine/phone.ts, unchanged in shape). Black box: reads replies, binds one to the live offer by hash, blesses or dismisses idempotently. Carries F15.

STANDING CONSTRAINTS, not elements: F13 report-the-attempt sits over E1-E3 - every announcement records its outcome; F14 withhold-the-credential sits over E2 - the store's token is read from the environment at the moment of use and never enters an argument, a record or a message.
payload.allocation_exact: Fifteen functions, fifteen allocations, none split and none doubled. F1, F2 -> E1. F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F12 -> E2. F8, F9, F10, F11 -> E3. F15 -> E4. F13, F14 -> the standing constraints. The one that could plausibly have been double-allocated is F12 degrade-deliberately: E3 also continues when E2 fails, but E3 simply receives an absent input - the DECISION to continue without a brief belongs to E2's contract of never failing outward, so F12 sits there alone.
payload.interfaces_both_ends:
Three interfaces, each declared at both ends.

I1 E1 -> E2/E3, THE PERMISSION AND THE PAIRING. Declared by E1 as what it emits (announce or stay silent, plus the current settings) and by both consumers as what they require. Mandatory: if E1 says stay silent, neither runs.

I2 E2 -> E3, THE BRIEF URL. Declared by E2 as its only output and by E3 as an OPTIONAL input. Deliberately asymmetric and the only optional interface in the design - E3 must be complete without it. This single edge is the ladder.

I3 E3 -> E4, THE ANSWER TOPIC. Declared by E3 as the address it puts on the actions and by E4 as the address it reads. Symmetric because both derive it from the same pairing through the same absolutization rule - which is exactly the symmetry that was broken before, when the card wrote a scheme-like token and the reader expected a topic.

No interface is declared at one end only, and no element reaches inside another: E3 never asks why E2 returned nothing, and E2 never learns whether a card was sent.
